Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, CTO; Morgan Patel, Chief Revenue Officer; Casey Nguyen, Chief Product Officer; and Riley Thompson, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on seven key areas: new customer acquisition, CAC trends, expansion revenue, ARR growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, gross margin, operating margin, and churn analysis.

Starting with new customer acquisition, which remains a cornerstone of our growth engine in the hyper-competitive SaaS landscape. CloudForge provides an AI-enhanced DevOps platform that streamlines CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, and collaborative development workflows—think GitLab meets Harness, but with proprietary ML-driven predictive analytics for deployment optimization.

In Q2, we added 1,450 net new customers, marking a 28% quarter-over-quarter increase from the 1,130 added in Q1 and a robust 52% year-over-year growth from the 950 in Q2 FY2023. This acceleration reflects the maturation of our product-led growth motion, where self-serve onboarding via our freemium tier has lowered barriers to entry, particularly for SMBs and mid-market teams. Breaking it down by segment:

Enterprise, with ACV over $100k, saw 185 new logos, up 35% QoQ, driven by multi-year deals averaging $245k DACV. Key wins included three Fortune 500 names in fintech—similar to how Datadog landed JPMorgan—and expansions into healthcare with HIPAA-compliant modules.

Mid-market, ACV $25k to $100k, added 620 customers, our highest growth bucket at 42% YoY, fueled by targeted outbound sales and partnerships with AWS Marketplace and Snowflake's ecosystem.

SMB and self-serve, ACV under $25k, brought in 645 new customers, representing 44% of total adds, with conversion from free to paid hitting 18%—ahead of our internal target of 15% and in line with PLG leaders like HubSpot.

This cohort diversity is deliberate, mitigating churn risk while maximizing land-and-expand potential. Our average DACV for new customers came in at $42.7k, a 12% improvement YoY, thanks to upmarket shifts and bundling of our new ForgeAI Predict module, which uses generative AI to forecast pipeline bottlenecks with 92% accuracy—early adopters are seeing 30% faster release cycles.

These 1,450 new customers contributed $18.4 million in new ARR, equivalent to $1.53 million in new MRR. This represents 62% of our total Q2 ARR growth of $29.7 million, underscoring acquisition as the primary driver amid a macro environment where logos are harder-won than expansions. Sequentially, new ARR grew 32% from Q1's $13.9 million, outpacing the SaaS industry average of 20-25% as reported by Bessemer Venture Partners' Cloud Index.

To put this in perspective: Total ARR ended Q2 at $428 million, up 41% YoY. New ARR as a percentage of total ARR stood at 4.3%, strong for our $400M+ ARR tier, comparable to ServiceNow's cohort metrics. Phased impact: Q2 new ARR will fully annualize by Q4, projecting an additional $12-15M tailwind into FY2025, assuming our historical 105-110% NRR.

Regionally, performance was geographically balanced: North America with 68% of adds at 985 customers, with California and New York leading due to tech hub density and integrations with Google Cloud's Vertex AI. EMEA at 22% share with 320 adds, up 65% YoY on GDPR-ready features and wins with Siemens and BNP Paribas—addressing the region's slower sales cycles via localized partner programs with Inchcape Digital. APAC at 10% with 145 adds, accelerating 80% YoY via Singapore HQ expansion and Tencent Cloud co-sell agreements; Japan and India showed particular strength in gaming and e-commerce verticals.

Strategically, several initiatives propelled this outperformance: Technical roadmap execution with the ForgeAI launch in May driving 40% of enterprise deals, A/B testing showing 2.5x higher conversion from trial to paid versus legacy features, and deepening integrations with Kubernetes 1.29 and Terraform 1.6, reducing setup time by 50%. Go-to-market optimization refining our ICP to DevOps leads at Series B+ startups and enterprises with over 500 engineers, yielding a 3x ROI on our $8M Q2 marketing spend with CAC payback under 9 months. Partner ecosystem contributing 25% of new ARR, including our first hyperscaler joint go-to-market with Azure DevOps, mirroring Snowflake's partner-led surge. Economic tailwinds where despite SaaS budget scrutiny—per Gartner, 2024 IT spend growth tempered to 8%—our ROI story resonates: customers report 25-35% OpEx savings on manual QA, critical in a high-interest-rate world.

Looking ahead, we guide to 1,600-1,800 net new customers in Q3, implying $20-23M new ARR, supported by Q3 AI feature drops and EMEA field expansion. Risks include elongated enterprise sales cycles now at 120 days versus 90 historical and competition from open-source alternatives like ArgoCD, but our proprietary moat in predictive analytics positions us well.

Next, on CAC trends, which continue to reflect the strong operating leverage we're driving across our go-to-market engine. For Q2, our blended CAC came in at $1,075, marking a 14% sequential decline from $1,250 in Q1 and a robust 22% year-over-year improvement from $1,380 in Q2 last year. This puts us well ahead of the SaaS industry median of around $1,200 for mid-market enterprise workflow automation players, based on recent Bessemer Venture Partners' benchmarks.

Breaking it down by acquisition channel, paid channels including SEM on Google and LinkedIn, as well as programmatic display, accounted for 42% of new customers and delivered a CAC of $1,850—down 18% QoQ thanks to our AI-driven bid optimization platform, built in-house using reinforcement learning models similar to those powering Adobe's advertising stack. This improved our cost-per-lead by 25% while maintaining a 3.2% conversion rate from lead to closed-won.

Organic and product-led growth channels—spanning SEO, content syndication via partnerships like G2 and Capterra, and our freemium self-serve tier—drove 35% of acquisitions at a stellar $620 CAC, with costs down 11% due to viral loop enhancements in our CloudForge Workflow app. We've seen our K-factor hit 1.35 here, fueled by seamless integrations with Slack and Microsoft Teams, mirroring the PLG flywheels at companies like Notion and HubSpot. Partnerships and channel resellers, including our expanded AWS Marketplace presence and co-sell agreements with Snowflake, rounded out the rest at $980 CAC, with a 20% QoQ ramp from new OEM deals.

Regionally, North America, our core market representing 58% of new ARR, saw CAC tick down 12% QoQ to $1,300 amid fierce competition from incumbents like ServiceNow and UiPath, but we're gaining share through targeted account-based marketing campaigns yielding 4x ROI on our top 500 enterprise logos. EMEA saw the sharpest drop—22% QoQ to $850—benefiting from GDPR-compliant inbound strategies and a new localization push in Germany and the UK, where we've doubled our German-speaking sales reps and seen organic search traffic surge 40% post our Workflow Compliance Hub content series. APAC CAC held steady at $1,100, flat QoQ but down 15% YoY, as our investments in Japan and Australia via Tencent Cloud partnerships start to scale, though we're still navigating pricing sensitivity in a post-layoff macro environment reminiscent of Zoom's early APAC challenges. LATAM remains our efficiency outlier at $750 CAC, up 30% in volume QoQ from Mercado Libre integrations.

These improvements are translating directly to Rule of 40 discipline. Our LTV/CAC ratio expanded to 4.2x from 3.5x a year ago, assuming a conservative 48-month customer lifetime and $48,000 median ACV—well above the 3:1 gold standard. CAC payback has compressed to 9.2 months from 12.4 months YoY, giving us ample room to invest in growth even as we lap tougher comps. Our sales efficiency, via the Magic Number, printed at 0.92 for the quarter—comfortably efficient per KeyBanc's framework.

Looking forward, we expect Q3 blended CAC to decline another 8-10% sequentially as PLG scales to 40% of mix and our AI lead scoring—now integrating OpenAI's embeddings for 22% better MQL-to-SQL conversion—ramps fully. We're doubling down on brand-building initiatives, allocating 15% of SM spend to upper-funnel video series on YouTube and TikTok for IT decision-makers, akin to Snowflake's Data Cloud narrative success. This positions us for sub-$1,000 CAC at scale by FY25, even as we expand into adjacent verticals like fintech compliance, where early pilots show 2x faster sales cycles.

Overall, these trends underscore our GTM maturation in a disciplined macro—efficient acquisition fueling durable ARR growth.

Turning to expansion revenue from existing customers, one of our most critical growth engines in the SaaS world, where customer acquisition costs remain high—averaging $1.50 to $2.00 per dollar of ARR, per Bessemer Venture Partners' latest Cloud Index—this drives our dollar-based net retention rate, or NRR, which speaks directly to product stickiness, land-and-expand scalability, and long-term LTV.

In Q2, expansion revenue hit $28.2 million, representing 18.7% of our total revenue of $150.8 million. That's up 42% year-over-year from $19.8 million in Q2 FY2023, and sequentially up 11% from Q1's $25.4 million. This performance pushed our trailing 12-month NRR to 118%, meaning our existing customer base is generating 18% more ARR today than it did a year ago—well above the 110%+ threshold that top-quartile SaaS companies like Snowflake and ServiceNow consistently target for sustained hypergrowth.

Granular breakdown: Upsells to higher tiers at $11.3 million, or 40% of expansion, fueled by customers upgrading from Core to Enterprise, often adding advanced features like our ForgeAI predictive analytics suite. ACV on these upsells averaged $145,000, a 25% increase YoY, as enterprises layer on AI-driven modules amid the generative AI boom—think capabilities similar to Salesforce Einstein or Databricks' Lakehouse AI.

Cross-sells into adjacent modules at $8.5 million, or 30%, with strong attach rates with our new DevSecOps toolkit and DataForge warehouse connector. Notably, 65% came from customers who started with our flagship collaboration platform, expanding into security and analytics—mirroring the cross-sell playbook that powered Zoom's post-pandemic NRR surge to 130%.

Seat and usage expansions at $8.4 million, or 30%, pure volume growth, with average seat count per account up 22% YoY to 1,450 users. Our consumption-based pricing on API calls and storage—pegged to hyperscaler rates—kicked in here, especially as workloads scaled with remote-hybrid work trends persisting into 2024.

Regionally, North America at 62% of expansion revenue, or $17.5 million, driven by Fortune 500 names in tech and finance deepening deployments. EMEA grew 55% YoY to $6.8 million (24% share), thanks to GDPR-compliant AI features resonating with EU regulators and banks like those in the DACH region. APAC at 14% or $4.0 million, accelerated 68% YoY on wins in Japan and Australia, where we've invested in local data sovereignty via AWS Tokyo and Sydney regions—offsetting some macro headwinds like China's regulatory tightening.

Powering these trends: AI-first roadmap acceleration, with post-ForgeAI launch 72% of expansions now including AI modules, boosting median expansion velocity from 6 to 4 months, akin to how HubSpot's AI tools drove their NRR to 112% last quarter. Seamless ecosystem integrations with Snowflake, dbt, and Fivetran reducing time-to-value by 40%, enabling platform flywheels where data pipelines auto-scale usage. Customer Success 2.0, doubling our CSMs to 250, implementing quarterly business reviews with expansion playbooks—yielding a 15% lift in multi-product adoption, per our internal cohort analysis.

This underscores our bowling alley approach: start narrow with collaboration tools, then expand horizontally into full-stack DevOps and analytics. In a market where median SaaS NRR has dipped to 105% amid economic caution per KeyBanc's Q2 SaaS Survey, our 118% positions us for 25-30% organic growth in FY2025, even as we guide new logo adds at $65-70 million quarterly.

We expect Q3 expansion to land at $30-32 million, with NRR holding at 117-120%, assuming continued AI tailwinds and no major macro shocks. Our customer base of 3,200+ accounts, with 85% gross retention, gives us immense optionality.

On ARR growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, our north star metric as a mission-critical DevOps platform. As of the end of Q2 FY2024, our total ARR reached $428 million, marking a robust 7.5% quarter-over-quarter increase from $398 million at the end of Q1. On a year-over-year basis, this represents an impressive 41% growth from $302 million in Q2 FY2023—comfortably exceeding our guided range of 35-38% and outpacing the broader SaaS industry average of around 25-30% as reported in recent Bessemer Venture Partners' State of the Cloud indices.

Key ARR components: New logo ARR contribution at $18.4 million this quarter, up 32% QoQ, driven by 1,450 net new logos with an average ACV of $42.7k—our strongest yet. This includes several large wins, such as multi-year deals with Fortune 500 fintechs adopting our AI-optimized CI/CD pipelines for Kubernetes-orchestrated microservices, and expansions into healthcare.

Expansion ARR net expansions contributed around $18 million, or roughly 60% of total QoQ growth, reflecting a dollar-based NRR of 118% for the quarter, consistent with our trailing 12-month NRR of 118%. This land-and-expand motion shines, fueled by upsells into ForgeAI, which automates pipeline debugging and resource optimization—now live for 65% of our customer base and delivering 30-40% faster build times per early adopter feedback. Strength from existing customers in fintech and e-commerce, expanding seat counts and adding premium modules amid surging demand for observability-integrated DevOps.

Churn and contraction limited, with gross revenue retention at 98%, contraction to just 1.2% of ARR, primarily from a few mid-market SMBs navigating economic headwinds. Our focus on enterprise-grade SLAs and 99.99% uptime keeps churn below 5% annualized, ahead of peers like GitLab or Harness.

Regionally, North America accounts for 62% of total ARR at approximately $265 million, with 41% YoY growth propelled by federal sector wins under our FedRAMP Moderate authorization—large-scale DoD contractors accelerating cloud-native transformations. EMEA at 23% or $98 million, surged 55% YoY, bolstered by GDPR-compliant features and partnerships with AWS EMEA and OVHcloud, including a landmark deal with a major German automotive OEM. APAC now 12% at $51 million, grew 80% YoY but steady QoQ; our Singapore and Tokyo expansions and integrations with Alibaba Cloud position us for 20% of ARR from the region by FY2025 end.

This ARR trajectory validates our pivot toward AI-infused DevOps amid the generative AI boom—much like Snowflake embedding AI into data warehousing or Atlassian's Compass streamlining developer workflows. Investments in ForgeAI, including proprietary ML models for predictive failure detection, have shortened sales cycles by 20% in pilots and driven a 2.5x increase in inbound leads from Gartner Magic Quadrant shortlisters. We've layered in zero-trust security enhancements to counter rising cyber threats, resonating in regulated verticals.

We expect Q3 ARR growth in the 8-10% QoQ range, implying full-year FY2024 ARR of approximately $475-480 million and 38-40% YoY growth. This assumes continued macro resilience, but we're prudently factoring in elongated enterprise sales cycles industry-wide post-rate hikes. Our strong balance sheet—with $450 million in cash and minimal debt—gives us ample runway to double down on R&D at 26% of revenue and go-to-market expansion.

Now, gross margin continues to reflect the scalability and efficiency inherent in our SaaS model. For Q2 FY2024, we delivered a GAAP gross margin of 82.5%, up 130 basis points sequentially from 81.2% in Q1 and 270 basis points year-over-year from 79.8% in Q2 FY2023. On a non-GAAP basis, excluding stock-based compensation and amortization of acquired intangibles, our gross margin expanded to 84.1%, marking our 11th consecutive quarter of sequential improvement.

This strong performance underscores the leverage as our ARR scales past $400 million, up 41% year-over-year. Key drivers: Economies of scale in cloud infrastructure, the largest contributor at roughly 200 basis points YoY. Our platform—powered by ForgeAI analytics and core collaboration tools akin to next-gen Slack-Salesforce—relies on hyperscalers like AWS and Azure. In Q2, we realized benefits from multi-year migration to AWS Graviton ARM-based instances, up to 40% better price-performance on compute workloads. Optimized Kubernetes across 15 global regions with predictive autoscaling via our ML ops reduced idle capacity by 25% QoQ. This drove hosting and bandwidth costs, 45% of total COGS, down to 12.4% of revenue from 13.8% a year ago.

Product mix shift toward higher-margin offerings added 100 basis points. Self-serve and mid-market tiers, now 44% of ARR up from 35%, carry margins north of 90% with minimal pro services. Enterprise deals include some implementation, but upsell of ForgeAI—like generative AI copilot for real-time dashboarding—tilts mix favorably. Customers like major financial services firms are expanding from basic collab to full AI stacks, boosting cohort margins.

Regionally, North America at 86%, fueled by mature self-serve. EMEA grew ARR strongly but slight drag from localization for GDPR data sovereignty in Frankfurt and Paris. APAC held at 78%, offset by bandwidth in India and Japan where video collab surges 60% with hybrid work.

Headwinds: 80 basis points from FX volatility with strengthening USD on non-USD colo in Europe. R&D-led zero-trust security elevated pro services to 18% of COGS temporarily. These are strategic; NRR ex-expansion hit 102%.

We expect Q3 GAAP gross margin at 82.7% to 83.2%, expanding to low-80s high-teens by year-end as ARR nears $500 million. This positions us against Snowflake and Datadog, with 40% Rule of 40. Focus on AI-infused efficiency—next serverless inference for ForgeAI to shave 10-15% off costs—and 5-7% pricing uplifts on renewals.

Operating margin performance reflects our business model strength and disciplined cost leverage amid robust revenue growth. For Q2 FY2024, we delivered 28.4%, up 320 basis points YoY from 25.1%, and 110 basis points sequentially from 27.3% in Q1. This marks our 7th consecutive quarter of expansion, trailing twelve-month at 27.8%. Calculated as operating income over total revenue, it shows conversion of top-line to bottom-line—a hallmark of leaders like Adobe and ServiceNow sustaining above 30%.

Breakdown: Gross margin expansion at 82.5% provided foundation, driven by AWS Graviton migration yielding 22% compute cost reduction. Non-GAAP 84.1% from lower pro services as self-serve hits 45% net new ARR, cutting deployment 18% QoQ.

Sales and marketing efficiency: S&M to 32.1% from 35.4% YoY, thanks to Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader debut driving 40% MQL increase from inbound PLG at 28% new logos. CAC payback to 16 months from 19, sales velocity up 15% enterprise. North America upsell NRR 118% with AI add-ons.

R&D at 18.7% flat YoY, focused high-ROI: Generative AI from OpenAI/Anthropic enabling no-code agents automating 35% more tasks, driving record 125% NRR quarterly. Pilots show 3x ROI in six months like Datadog observability.

G&A efficient at 7.2% down from 8.1%, zero-based budgeting, India offshore 40% support at 98% CSAT.

Regionally, EMEA 18% revenue grew 45% YoY, margins to 26% on pricing amid Eurozone recovery. APAC 7% revenue at 22% margins investing local DCs, Japan bookings up 60% IoT integrations.

Expect Q3 29-30%, toward 35% long-term at $1B ARR. Assumes Rule of 60, AI NRR >120%, no macro shocks. $450M cash offsets R&D for quantum-safe encryption.

Finally, churn analysis, a cornerstone of financial health in SaaS amid macro headwinds and competition from Salesforce Einstein or HubSpot Breeze AI equivalents in DevOps. Managing churn drives NRR for growth. Q2 gross dollar churn 4.2%, down 150 bps YoY from 5.7%, flat seq from 4.3%. Annualized 16%, below 20-25% CRM/DevOps median per Bessemer. Logo churn 6.1%, but NRR 118% from 28% expansion via Predictive Lead Scoring analog in DevOps. 2023 cohorts churn 3.8% quarterly, 20% better.

Drivers from 142 lost accounts (~$4.2M ARR): Economic/budget 42%, mid-market cost optimization like Workday peers, 22% contractions. Competitive 28%, 40% to incumbents, 25% SMB rivals, feature gaps 15%. Product fit/usability 20%, NPS 68 up YoY, onboarding/integration lags. Support/renewals 10%, EMEA peak seasons.

Regional: NA 3.7% strong enterprise. EMEA 6.8% GDPR/econ lag. APAC 5.2% FX.

Mitigations: CS overhaul 1:80 ratio, QBRs for at-risk cut reactive 35%, CSAT 92%, ROI dashboards 3.8x LTV:CAC. AI churn prediction 87% accuracy on Snowflake/Databricks, rescues 24% predicted, $1.1M ARR back. Product: ForgeAI Insights 95% accurate recs, 15% expansions, 50+ integrations API marketplace cut switch 40%, usage pricing pilots. Regional: EMEA local compliance/VARs cut 12% QoQ, APAC localization. Pricing: Evergreen renewals +5 NRR pts, incentives close 62% at-risk.

Embeds deeper into revenue ops workflows like Snowflake consumption. LTV $450K mid-market up YoY, payback <9 months. Q3 churn to 4.0%, NRR 120%. High-ACV enterprise 40% bookings resilient.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss the financials in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $150.8 million, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82.5%, and operating income was $42.8 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at $450 million, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $620 million to $640 million.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim for a technology update.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Casey Nguyen will provide update on product roadmap.

Casey Nguyen:
Thank you, Taylor. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of ForgeAI Predict. This new feature significantly improves deployment forecasting and pipeline optimization. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature which aligns with our product strategy.

Riley Thompson:
Thank you, Casey. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 35% increase in website traffic and a 28% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, and what's the competitive landscape like?

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI has been a game-changer for our overall growth, contributing to over 40% of new enterprise deals and accelerating our NRR to 118%. We're seeing attach rates of around 72% among existing customers who have trialed it, with upsell velocity improving by 33% quarter-over-quarter. This has exceeded our initial expectations, where we modeled for 50-60% adoption in year one; we're already at 65% platform-wide. Competitively, our proprietary predictive analytics give us a clear moat against open-source like ArgoCD and incumbents like GitLab, as evidenced by 2.5x higher trial-to-paid conversions in A/B tests. Customers value the 92% bottleneck forecast accuracy and 30% faster releases.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, and what are your expected ROI from these investments?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, Lisa. International expansion is a top priority, with APAC as a key focus given its 80% YoY growth this quarter. Plans include doubling our Singapore HQ team, launching a Tokyo data center, and deepening Tencent and Alibaba co-sells. Key target markets are Japan for manufacturing and gaming, India for e-commerce and startups, and Australia for fintech—representing high-growth verticals with strong DevOps needs. We expect ROI of 3-4x within 18 months, based on current CAC payback under 10 months there and pilots showing 60% faster sales cycles post-localization. This should drive APAC to 20% of ARR by FY2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, and what's the impact of pricing changes on churn?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Mike. In this environment, we're managing churn proactively at 4.2% gross dollar, down YoY, with NRR trending at 118% TTM—stable and above peers. Strategies include AI-powered prediction rescuing 24% of at-risk accounts, CS overhauls with 1:80 ratios and QBRs cutting reactive churn 35%, and product innovations like ForgeAI Insights boosting expansions 15%. Pricing changes, like 5-7% renewal uplifts and Evergreen auto-expansions, have added 5 NRR points without increasing churn, as LTV rises to $450k with <9 month payback. Enterprise focus at 40% bookings keeps us resilient.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
